--- title: "Linearity and group heterogeneity diagnostics for the Declared × Assessed inference" description: "Which inference does the December 2025 certificate cross-section support: a linear logit, a spline logit, quantile regression of the balance, or a mixed logit?" date: 2026-11-04 jupyter: python3 --- **Data.** December 2025 snapshot (`MES_EXTRACAO = 12`, as of 2025-12-31) of declared and assessed VAT (ICMS) certificates. Payments are GARE amounts dated before 1 January 2026. Firm attributes come from the March 2026 CNPJ register already joined in section 3.15. The unit is the certificate (CDA). **Question.** The declared × assessed paper needs one inference before the EAA deadline of 1 December 2026. This page fits the candidate specifications on the same sample and ends with the specification the diagnostics support. **Status.** The computation is `analyze.py` in the folder of the same name. Render this page on the machine that has the extract. The cloud copy runs the same functions on synthetic rows and does not read the extract. ::: {.callout-note title="Render on the machine with the disk"} The page checks the section 3.15 counts before it fits anything. This diagnostic is section 4.5. Section 4.2 remains the monthly series against macroeconomic indicators. ::: {#load-sample .cell execution_count=1} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` load-sample: 13.3 s population CDAs: declared 2257189, assessed 59542 eligible CDAs before the sample: 2313681 estimation sample drawn: 200000 ``` ::: ::: ::: {#ols-reset .cell execution_count=2} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` quantile regression rows: 20000 ols-reset full: 14.4 s ``` ::: ::: ::: {#splines .cell execution_count=3} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` spline cache: miss splines: 0.7 s spline cache: miss ``` ::: ::: ::: {#icc-mixed .cell execution_count=4} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` mixed cache municipality: miss mixed cache division: miss icc-mixed: 13.0 s mixed cache: miss ``` ::: ::: ::: {#top1 .cell execution_count=5} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` ols-reset trim: 12.1 s ``` ::: ::: ## Sample The population is every declared and assessed certificate in the December 2025 snapshot. The fits use a stratified sample of at most 200,000 complete cases. Strata are segment × firm size × any payment. DuckDB spills to `/tmp` with a 900 MB memory limit. The sensitivity sample drops the largest 1 percent of that estimation sample by stock, `ceil(0.01 × n)` certificates. A cell with fewer than 10 certificates or fewer than 5 firms is left blank. Municipality rows carry the municipality name and the UF only. ::: {#tbl-population .cell tbl-cap='Population counts checked against section 3.15 segment_summary.csv, and the estimation sample.' execution_count=6} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Declared: 2,257,189 certificates, stock R$116.42 billion. Assessed: 59,542 certificates, stock R$311.40 billion. Eligible complete cases: 2,313,681. Estimation sample: 200,000. After dropping the top 1 percent: 198,000. Share of the estimation sample with UF = SP: 0.850. ``` ::: ::: ## Outcomes and regressors Two outcomes, both ordinary least squares with HC3 standard errors (MacKinnon and White 1985) and, as a second column, standard errors clustered by the 8-digit CNPJ root. Stock, the main outcome: $$ \log(1 + S_i) = x_i^\top\beta + \varepsilon_i $$ Recovery, the second outcome: $$ R_i = P_i / S_i = x_i^\top\gamma + u_i $$ $S_i$ is the December 2025 stock net of legal fees. $P_i$ is the sum of GARE payments dated before 1 January 2026. $\log(1+S_i)$ is defined for every positive stock. Section 5.6.1, on the certificate-year panel, is $$ \operatorname{logit}\Pr(Y_{it}=1) = \alpha + \beta_1\log S_{it} + \beta_2\mathrm{age}_{it} + \beta_3 r_{i,t-1} + \delta_t. $$ This page is one cross-section, so the year effect $\delta_t$ and the lagged recovery $r_{i,t-1}$ are not in the design. Debt age is that model's age, in years, unlogged. Log stock is the stock outcome, and it is a regressor of recovery and of the payment logit. The added regressors are segment (declared as the reference), CNAE section (G, trade, as the reference when it is present) and firm size (Micro, code 01, as the reference when it is present). ::: {#formulas .cell execution_count=7} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` log_stock ~ debt_age + C(segment, Treatment(reference='declared')) + C(section, Treatment(reference='G')) + C(porte, Treatment(reference='01')) recovery ~ log_stock + debt_age + C(segment, Treatment(reference='declared')) + C(section, Treatment(reference='G')) + C(porte, Treatment(reference='01')) ``` ::: ::: ## Linear estimates **How to read the coefficient tables.** One row per term. `coef_full` and `se_full` are the estimation sample. `coef_trim` and `se_trim` drop the top 1 percent by stock. The HC3 table is the one used for the decision. The cluster table is the same point estimates with a different standard error. An interval that covers zero is compatible with no partial association at this specification. The $R^2$ is the share of variance of the outcome linearly associated with $x$, in this sample. It is not an out-of-sample fit, and it is not a structural elasticity. ::: {#tbl-stock-hc3 .cell tbl-cap='OLS of log(1+stock). HC3 standard errors. ``` ::: ::: ## Residual plots **How to read.** The colour in the residual plot is the number of certificates in a bin. The horizontal axis is the centre of a fitted-value bin and the vertical axis is the centre of a residual bin. Counts are computed in Python. A bin with fewer than 5 certificates is blank, so no certificate value is sent to the page. The grey line is a residual of zero. A fan means the occupied bins spread as the fitted value grows. A bend means the occupied bins leave the zero line. In the observed-against-fitted plot both axes are bin centres, in the outcome's units. The dashed line is the 45-degree line, the locus where the fitted value equals the observed value. Occupied bins that leave that line are a curved conditional mean. Bins that spread away from the line are heteroskedasticity, which HC3 already targets. The decision treats a Spearman correlation of at least 0.20 between the absolute residual and the fitted value, computed on the certificates and not drawn, as a material fan. The normal quantile plot has 40 theoretical normal quantiles on the horizontal axis and the matching quantiles of the residual distribution on the vertical axis. It is not a point per certificate. The dashed line goes through the quartiles of those 40 quantiles. Departure from that line is a departure from a normal residual, which does not by itself reject a linear mean. The first figure of each pair is the full estimation sample. The second drops the top 1 percent by stock. ::: {#fig-stock-residual .cell execution_count=11} ::: {#fig-stock-residual-1 .cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ## RESET and Harvey–Collier Ramsey's RESET (1969) adds the square and the cube of the fitted values to the linear equation and tests those two terms with an $F$ statistic (`power=3`, `use_f=True`). The HC3 variant uses the same added terms with a heteroskedasticity-consistent covariance (White 1980; MacKinnon and White 1985). The Harvey–Collier statistic is the one already used in section 4.2: a test that the mean of the recursive residuals is zero. The partial $R^2$ is the gain in $R^2$ from those two powers. At this sample size a small $p$-value is cheap. The decision uses a partial $R^2$ of at least 0.01, or a rank correlation of at least 0.20 between the absolute residual and the fitted value. Both cuts are working assumptions, listed under Premissas. **How to read.** One row per outcome, sample and segment. `pooled` uses both segments. `declared` and `assessed` drop the segment indicator and refit inside the segment. `reset_p` is the classical $F$ test. `reset_p_hc3` is the HC3 version. `harvey_p` is the Harvey–Collier $p$-value, missing when the recursion is not defined. ::: {#tbl-reset .cell tbl-cap='RESET and Harvey–Collier statistics for both outcomes, both samples, pooled and by segment.' execution_count=19} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ## Payment log-odds, bins and splines The binary outcome is any payment, $P_i > 0$, the same definition as section 3.15. Inside each segment, log stock and debt age are cut into 20 quantile bins. The empirical log-odds in a bin with $k$ payers out of $n$ certificates is the Haldane–Anscombe estimator $$ \hat\lambda = \log\frac{k+1/2}{n-k+1/2}, \qquad \mathrm{se}(\hat\lambda) = \sqrt{\frac{1}{k+1/2}+\frac{1}{n-k+1/2}}. $$ The interval is $\hat\lambda \pm 1.96\,\mathrm{se}(\hat\lambda)$. It stays finite when $k=0$ and when $k=n$. On the same certificates, two logits are fit for each variable, separately in Declared and in Assessed: a straight line in that variable, and a restricted cubic spline with 4 degrees of freedom (Durrleman and Simon 1989, via `cr()`). The likelihood-ratio statistic compares the two maximised log-likelihoods. ΔAIC is the linear AIC minus the spline AIC, so a positive value favours the spline. For that segment and that variable, the spline is used when ΔAIC is at least 10 or the spline log-odds are not monotone on the 5th-to-95th percentile grid. A segment whose ΔAIC stays below 10 and whose spline is monotone keeps the linear logit. Firm size and registration status are categories: the log-odds are reported by level, and the only shape question for size is whether Micro, Small and Other sizes rise in that order. A level with 1 to 4 payers is left blank. **How to read the figure.** The horizontal axis is the midpoint of the quantile bin (the average of the bin edges). The vertical axis is the payment log-odds. Dots are the bin estimates, with the 95 percent interval. A dotted line is the linear logit. A solid line is the spline logit. Declared is teal and assessed is orange. A line that turns while the dots turn with it is curvature of the payment log-odds. A line that turns while the dots stay flat is the spline using degrees of freedom the bins do not support. Bins with fewer than 10 certificates or 5 firms are omitted. ::: {#cell-fig-logodds-stock .cell execution_count=20} ::: {#fig-logodds-stock .cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ## Group heterogeneity Two groupings are summarised: the CNAE division (two digits) and the municipality. The UF is not a grouping factor. The debtors sit in São Paulo, so the state has almost no variation; the share with UF = SP is printed with the sample. For each group the table reports the number of certificates, the number of firms, the payment rate and the Haldane–Anscombe log-odds. The funnel compares each group's rate to the binomial limits around the pooled rate $\pi$, $$ \pi \pm z\sqrt{\pi(1-\pi)/n}, $$ with $z = 1.96$ (95 percent) and $z = \Phi^{-1}(0.999)$ (99.8 percent). Limits are the sampling noise of a common rate. A point outside the 99.8 percent limit is more dispersed than that noise. The latent intraclass correlation for a binary outcome is $$ \mathrm{ICC} = \frac{\tau^2}{\tau^2 + \pi^2/3}, $$ as in Goldstein, Browne and Rasbash (2002). The screen is a method-of-moments $\tau^2$: the variance of group payment rates, minus the binomial sampling variance, divided by $[\pi(1-\pi)]^2$. It is computed on the full estimation sample, separately for Declared and for Assessed, and it is the ICC that selects the mixed logit. The classical ICC of log stock and of recovery is the unbalanced one-way random-intercept ANOVA. A variational random-intercept logit is a supporting estimate. It is fit only when the moment ICC is at least 0.05, on a cluster sample: whole municipalities or divisions are drawn, with at most 30 certificates from each, until 8,000 certificates. A row-wise sample would leave a handful of certificates in each municipality and shrink $\tau^2$. The variational ICC can still be biased when groups are smaller than 30 or when a large group is capped at 30. It does not select the mixed logit. A second fit adds the payment-equation controls when the null variational ICC stays at or above 0.05. **How to read the funnel and the table.** The horizontal axis is the number of certificates in the group. The vertical axis is the payment rate. Each point is one municipality or one CNAE division, not one certificate. The grey curves are the 99.8 percent limits around the pooled rate. The page draws and lists only groups outside those limits, and at most the 50 largest of them in each grouping and segment. The count printed above the table is the number of groups in total, and how many of the publishable ones fall outside. Groups under 10 certificates, under 5 firms, or with 1 to 4 payers are not drawn and are not listed. A count of 1 to 4 is not printed. ::: {#cell-fig-funnel-municipality .cell execution_count=25} ::: {#fig-funnel-municipality .cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
